title: Time-Switching Energy-Harvesting Quantum Relay-Assisted FSO Communication with Displaced Squeezed Signaling
authors: Nizar Khalfet, Francisco A. Monteiro, Ioannis Krikidis
abstract: This paper investigates a quantum relay-assisted free-space optical (FSO) communication system in which a decode-and-forward relay is powered by time-switching optical energy harvesting and forwards the decoded information using displaced squeezed signaling (DSS). To obtain a physically con sistent description of turbulence-induced loss for non-classical signaling, each hop is modeled as a pure-loss bosonic chan nel whose random transmissivity follows a truncated Gamma Gamma law, i.e., the Gamma-Gamma irradiance conditioned on the physically admissible range of a transmittance. Under this channel, coherent states remain pure, whereas squeezed states are mapped to mixed Gaussian states. Under Helstrom-optimal detection, the average error of the coherent hop is derived in exact Laplace-series form. For the DSS hop, we derive the output states, a closed-form Gaussian fidelity with rigorous two sided bounds on the Helstrom error, and prove the existence of a loss-aware optimal photon partition. Furthermore, we prove that optimized squeezing preserves both the turbulence-induced diversity order and the leading asymptotic constant of coherent relaying, so that its benefit is a finite-photon-budget effect, and that an interior throughput-optimal harvesting fraction exists. A covariance-preserving benchmark with an exact series representation yields an analytical upper bound on the achievable throughput whose absolute gap vanishes as the relay photon budget grows. Numerical results based on the exact mixed-state Helstrom error quantify the benefit of squeezing and the regime in which it is useful.
summary: This work analyzes quantum communication over free-space optical links incorporating energy harvesting and atmospheric turbulence. It develops rigorous bounds for the achievable rate using displaced squeezed signaling and time-switching protocols. The findings demonstrate that quantum resources like squeezing offer tangible benefits even under realistic, energy-constrained, and lossy channel conditions.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified analytical framework for quantum relay-assisted Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication that must account for energy sustainability constraints, non-classical signaling, and atmospheric turbulence.
main_result: It derives performance metrics for time-switching energy-harvesting quantum relaying, proving that optimized squeezing provides a finite-photon-budget benefit and that the achievable throughput approaches an analytical upper bound as the photon budget increases.
method: The analysis uses Helstrom-optimal detection theory, modeling the communication hops as pure-loss bosonic channels governed by a truncated Gamma-Gamma random transmissivity.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum relay-assisted FSO link utilizing a time-switching decode-and-forward protocol. The relay is powered by energy harvested from the environment, and the quantum signal uses Displaced Squeezed Signaling (DSS).
key_observables: Average error (Helstrom error), achievable throughput, and the preservation of diversity order.
important_parameters: Time-switching fraction $t$, energy harvesting efficiency $\eta_{	ext{pv}}$, and the degree of squeezing.
main_assumptions: The turbulence-induced loss is modeled by a truncated Gamma-Gamma law, and the relay operates under an instantaneous energy-causality constraint.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the system model (EH, DSS, FSO hops), formulates the detection problem using Helstrom bounds, and presents the performance analysis by deriving closed-form fidelities and proving asymptotic bounds.
why_interesting: It combines quantum communication theory with realistic physical constraints (energy harvesting and atmospheric loss), providing advanced analytical tools for quantum networking in challenging environments.
